stories.title: S&P 500 jumps 1.60% to 7,297.49 in the Black Friday half-day; Nasdaq +2.31%
stories.body: At the 1:00 PM close the S&P 500 was 7,297.49 (+114.71, +1.60%), the Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50 (+2.31%), the Nasdaq-100 26,726.39 (+2.61%) and the Dow 50,774.94 (+591.99, +1.18%) (JBizNews, BigGo); the Russell 2000 ended at 2,750.30 (+1.71%) (Yahoo Finance). For the week the S&P 500 rose 5.6%, its biggest weekly gain since April 2025, the Dow 5.5% and the Nasdaq 6.7% (BigGo). The S&P 500 still closed 57 points under its 200-day average of 7,354.27 (Cestrian).
stories.why: The rebound stopped just below the 200-day average (Cestrian puts SPY's equivalent near $733), so Monday's first full session of completed 1-hour closes shows whether that level is cleared or rejected.

stories.title: Amazon +3.96% on Black Friday demand; Tesla +5.22% to $400
stories.body: Amazon closed at $254.12 (+3.96%) on Black Friday and Thanksgiving spending data: Adobe put Thanksgiving-day online spending at a record $7.1 billion, and Amazon extended its deals to 12 days (TipRanks). Tesla rose 5.22% to close at $400.00 after a report that it is pushing to buy a German maker of humanoid-robot parts (TipRanks). Apple ended at $358.54 (+0.83%) (BigGo) and Meta rose about 3.1% (Trading Economics). Adobe expects holiday online spending of $275.1 billion, up 6.7% (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: AMZN and TSLA closed near the highs of the half-day; with only about three completed 1-hour candles Friday, Monday's first full-session closes test whether the breakouts hold.

stories.title: Chip index +4.69%: AMD +4.56%, Broadcom +3.82%, while Nvidia lags at +0.80%
stories.body: The PHLX Semiconductor index closed at 9,186.71 (+4.69%) (JBizNews, BigGo). AMD ended at $424.54 (+4.56%), Broadcom $312.34 (+3.82%) and Nvidia $150.49 (+0.80%), reversing early losses (BigGo); Intel's last 1-hour close was $57.85 (+6.21%) (Structure One feed), with no stock-specific reason found. Nvidia lagged after reports it would halt chip orders to certain Southeast Asian countries and that Blackwell chips were installed in a Shanghai data center (Motley Fool); S&P Global has Nvidia's AA ratings on negative watch (BigGo).
stories.why: Chips bounced hard off Wednesday's lows, but NVDA's weak relative close shows the group is not moving as one; each name's own 1-hour closes matter more than the index.

stories.title: Banks and energy join the rally; JPMorgan +1.92% as Goldman and Morgan Stanley gain 2.5%
stories.body: Last 1-hour closes: JPM $322.82 (+1.92%), BAC $49.00 (+0.95%), XOM $160.52 (+1.54%), CVX $213.11 (+1.02%) (Structure One feed). Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs each rose 2.5% (Trading Economics), and bank shares including JPMorgan advanced (Reuters via STL.News). Energy outpaced most sectors (Motley Fool) even as WTI settled at $83.08, down 0.7% (Reuters via AOL).
stories.why: XOM and CVX rose while crude fell, so the energy names are not simply tracking oil; banks rose with the 10-year yield near 4.94%.

stories.title: Micron +7.60% to $646.95 as memory stocks bounce off a 40% monthly slide
stories.body: Micron closed at $646.95 (+7.60%) (BigGo, TipRanks). Investing.com said investors returned to AI-linked chipmakers after a pullback of nearly 40% over the past month on memory-oversupply fears and weaker NAND prices; Motley Fool called it an oversold bounce (citing StreetInsider), with the stock still 45% below its June peak. TrendForce said conventional DRAM prices may keep rising through 2027, at a slower pace (TipRanks). Micron's buyback window opens Dec. 9 and it reports fiscal Q1 2027 results Dec. 17 (Investing.com).
stories.why: MU has swung 7–13% intraday in recent sessions; a bounce from oversold levels can retrace quickly, so the first completed 1-hour closes Monday show whether buyers defend Friday's range.

stories.title: Silver +5.4% and gold heads for its first weekly rise in three weeks
stories.body: Spot gold was $3,635.81 at 9:34 AM ET, up nearly 2% and on track for a weekly gain of nearly 3%, with spot silver at $43.73 (+5.4%) (Reuters via Kitco). February gold futures ended at $3,671.30 (+2.31%) (Cestrian). Reuters cited bargain buying and physical demand in India and China, against a firm dollar, rising yields and a hawkish Fed outlook. Last 1-hour closes: GLD $332.75 (+1.62%), SLV $39.03 (+5.20%) (Structure One feed).
stories.why: Metals rose despite higher yields; SLV's 5% move in a half-day leaves a wide 1-hour range, and futures trade again before Monday's open.

stories.title: Brent slips 1.2% Friday but logs a weekly gain of about 3% on Saudi refinery strikes; OPEC+ meets Sunday
stories.body: WTI settled at $83.08, down 60 cents (0.7%), and Brent fell $1.13 (1.2%) to $95.44 after touching its highest since Nov. 9; for the week Brent rose about 3% and WTI fell 0.9% (Reuters via AOL). Reuters cited attacks on tankers near Hormuz and on Saudi energy sites: the Jazan refinery halted some operations after a projectile killed a worker Thursday, a day after Ras Tanura was attacked. OPEC+ is expected to keep Q1 2027 targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting, sources said. USO's last 1-hour close was $137.50 (−1.71%) and OXY $54.16 (+0.39%).
stories.why: The OPEC+ decision lands on Sunday, after Friday's last completed 1-hour close; USO and OXY can gap Monday on the outcome.

stories.title: VIX falls 11.16% to 23.81, down about a third on the week
stories.body: The VIX closed at 23.81, down 11.16% (Yahoo Finance, BigGo). Cestrian put it down 33.68% on the week from 35.90, with the MOVE bond-volatility index at 95.29 (−2.32%).
stories.why: Implied volatility is easing but still well above calm-market levels, so option premiums remain relatively expensive heading into the jobs report and the Fed meeting.

stories.title: 10-year yield rises to about 4.94%; futures still price a December hike
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.94% (Cestrian); Yahoo Finance showed 4.936%, up 8.8 bp, after the revised 4.3% Q3 GDP figure. Kitco cited futures pricing of about a 96% chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 8–9 Fed meeting, and JBizNews said CME FedWatch heavily favored a December increase. The bond market closed at 2:00 PM ET.
stories.why: Stocks rallied while yields rose; if yields keep climbing toward 5%, rate-sensitive names can lag the index in the 1-hour closes.

stories.title: Europe closes higher: DAX +0.87%, FTSE 100 +0.85% as miners lead
stories.body: The DAX closed 0.87% higher at 25,434, led by Rheinmetall (+3.17%) and Infineon (+3.15%), and the FTSE 100 rose 0.85% to 10,700 as miners led, with Antofagasta and Glencore up more than 4%. The CAC 40 rose 0.30% to 8,133 after French November inflation eased to 2.9% vs 3.2% expected (Trading Economics). Earlier, Asia closed sharply higher on the chip rebound: Nikkei 225 58,711.11 (+2.11%), KOSPI 4,915.68 (+4.34%) (NERO).
stories.why: Overseas chip and mining strength lined up with the US rebound; Asia's Monday session is the first read on whether it carries into next week.

stories.title: October goods trade deficit widens to $149.5B vs $133.1B expected
stories.body: The advance goods trade deficit was $149.5 billion in October vs $133.1 billion expected and $135.1 billion in September, as imports rose 6.1% to $365.3 billion and capital goods imports 8.5% to $171.4 billion. Wholesale inventories rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected, and retail inventories rose 0.8% (ActionForex). Before the data, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow was 2.9% for Q4, down from 3.2% (TipRanks). On Thanksgiving, President Trump called the revised 4.3% Q3 GDP figure "fake" (Yahoo Finance, citing Bloomberg).
stories.why: A wider deficit subtracts from GDP estimates; with a December hike already almost fully priced, the data matter more for yields than for stocks.

stories.title: S&P 500's 114.71-point gain topped the roughly 98-point move options priced for Friday's expiry
stories.body: At Wednesday's close options priced about a 1.37% (98.40-point) move for Friday's S&P 500 expiry, centred near 7,185, and the week's option-priced range topped out at 7,183.79; Nvidia's IV rank was 92.2 (Saxo). The index closed at 7,297.49, up 114.71 points (JBizNews), beyond both. Index options settled at the 1:00 PM close.
stories.why: A move larger than the priced range means short-premium positions lost on the expiry; next week's contracts start from a higher base with implied volatility still elevated.

stories.title: Ahead: OPEC+ Sunday, ISM Tuesday, jobs report Dec. 4, then the Fed and Broadcom on Dec. 9
stories.body: OPEC+ meets Sunday (Reuters via AOL). Monday brings the Chicago PMI at 9:45 AM (prior 55.3) and the Dallas Fed survey (Investing.com). Tuesday has ISM manufacturing (consensus 55.2) and JOLTS, Wednesday ADP (consensus 80,000), Thursday ISM services (54.5) and Friday, Dec. 4, November payrolls (consensus 90,000, unemployment 4.1%) (CalculatedRisk). Jensen Huang faces congressional hearings (Yahoo Finance). The Fed decides Dec. 9, when Broadcom reports after the close (Broadcom IR); Micron's buyback window opens Dec. 9 and it reports Dec. 17 (Investing.com).
stories.why: Weekend events (OPEC+) land after Friday's last completed 1-hour close, and the Dec. 4 jobs report is the main scheduled data before the Fed.
